verses.text: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were saying, "Jacob has taken everything our father owned. He has got all this wealth from what belonged to our father."
And Jacob noticed that Laban was no longer as friendly towards him as he had been before.
Then the LORD said to Jacob, "Go back to the land of your ancestors and to your relatives, and I will be with you."
So Jacob sent word to Rachel and Leah to come out to the fields where his flocks were.
He said to them, "I can see that your father is not as friendly towards me as he was before. But the God of my father has been with me.
You know that I have worked for your father as hard as I could.
Yet your father has cheated me by changing my pay ten times. But God has not let him harm me.

If he said, 'The speckled ones will be your pay', then all the flocks gave birth to speckled young. And if he said, 'The striped ones will be your pay', then all the flocks gave birth to striped young.
So God has taken away your father's livestock and given it to me.
Once, during the mating season, I had a dream. I looked up and saw that the male goats mating with the flock were striped, speckled or spotted.
The angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob.' I answered, 'Here I am.'
He said, 'Look up and see that all the male goats mating with the flock are striped, speckled or spotted, because I have seen everything Laban has been doing to you.
I am the God of Bethel, where you poured oil on a pillar and where you made a solemn promise to me. Now get ready to leave this land at once and go back to the land where you were born.'"
Then Rachel and Leah replied, "Do we still have any share in the inheritance of our father's estate?
Does he not treat us like foreigners? Not only has he sold us, but he has used up all the money that was paid for us.
Surely all the wealth that God took away from our father belongs to us and our children. So do whatever God has told you."
Then Jacob got ready and put his children and his wives on camels.
He drove all his livestock ahead of him, with all the goods he had gathered in Paddan Aram, and set out to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
While Laban had gone to cut the wool from his sheep, Rachel stole her father's household idols.
Jacob also tricked Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
So he ran away with everything he had. He crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead.
On the third day Laban was told that Jacob had run away.
He took his relatives with him and chased Jacob for seven days. He caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
Then God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and said to him, "Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad."
Jacob had set up his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban caught up with him. Laban and his relatives set up camp there too.
Then Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done? You have tricked me, and you have carried off my daughters like prisoners of war.
Why did you run away secretly and trick me? Why did you not tell me? I would have sent you off with joy and singing, with the music of tambourines and harps.
You did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. You have done a foolish thing.
I have the power to harm you. But last night the God of your father said to me, 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'
Now you have gone off because you longed so much to go back to your father's home. But why did you steal my gods?"
Jacob answered Laban, "I was afraid. I thought you would take your daughters away from me by force.

But if you find anyone who has your gods, that person will not live. Here, in front of our relatives, look for yourself and see if there is anything of yours with me, and if so, take it." Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the gods.
So Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the tent of the two slave women, but he found nothing. After he came out of Leah's tent, he went into Rachel's tent.
Now Rachel had taken the household idols and put them inside her camel's saddle, and she was sitting on them. Laban searched through everything in the tent but found nothing.
Rachel said to her father, "Please do not be angry, sir, that I cannot stand up in front of you. I am having my monthly period." So he searched but could not find the household idols.
Then Jacob became angry and argued with Laban. "What wrong have I done?" he asked Laban. "What sin have I committed, that you have chased after me so fiercely?
Now that you have searched through all my goods, what have you found that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of your relatives and mine, and let them judge between the two of us.
I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not lost their young, and I have not eaten any rams from your flocks.
I did not bring you animals torn apart by wild beasts. I paid for the loss myself. And you made me pay for whatever was stolen, whether by day or by night.
This is how it was for me: the heat wore me out in the daytime and the cold at night, and I could not sleep.
For twenty years I have been in your household. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and you changed my pay ten times.

If the God of my father, the God of Abraham, the God whom Isaac fears, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away with nothing. But God has seen my trouble and my hard work, and last night he warned you."

Laban answered Jacob, "The women are my daughters, the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks. Everything you see is mine. But what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have had?
Come now, let's make a covenant, you and I. Let it be a witness between us."
So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.
He said to his relatives, "Gather some stones." So they took stones and piled them in a heap, and they ate there beside the heap.
Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean "heap of witness".
Laban said, "This heap is a witness between you and me today." That is why it was called Galeed.
It was also called Mizpah, which means "watchtower", because he said, "May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are apart from each other.
If you treat my daughters badly, or if you marry other wives besides my daughters, remember that even though no one else is with us, God is a witness between you and me."
Laban also said to Jacob, "Here is this heap, and here is this pillar I have set up between you and me.
This heap is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this heap to harm you, and that you will not go past this heap and pillar to harm me.
May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." So Jacob made a solemn promise in the name of the God whom his father Isaac feared.
Jacob offered a sacrifice there in the hill country and invited his relatives to a meal. After they had eaten, they spent the night there.
Early the next morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then he left and went back home.
